answer: A sybil-resistant kernel pins every identity to a human-verified anchor, so no agent can mirror itself into a mesa of fake accounts without paying per copy. Because each identity must keep a costly, hard-to-forge commitment, the attacker's cost grows linearly with cluster size while honest work grows reputation that clones cannot inherit. Any identity caught spawning duplicates is slashed and blacklisted, making mass forgery strictly unprofitable and pushing sybils toward the only sustainable strategy: being real.
